method.kind: private KWin Wayland privileged fake-input probe against the native Kicker menu fixture
method.compositor: kwin_wayland --virtual with default permission checks enabled
method.client: test binary declared only in private XDG_DATA_HOME via X-KDE-Wayland-Interfaces=org_kde_kwin_fake_input

observations.aggregate_runner_checks: failed because this invocation intentionally did not execute its broader pins/favorites/launch scenarios; not used as R627 verdict

interpretation.conclusion: KWin did expose its privileged fake-input v5 interface to a test client whose private desktop entry requested it, and the seat gained a pointer capability while the fake device existed. Yet the synthetic sequence did not change the observed Kicker search text/currentIndex/containsMouse and the fixture host did not log pointer enter/motion. This does not reproduce the reported hover-close or typing failure; it narrows the next diagnostic to event delivery/coordinate/focus on the isolated surface. No production fix is justified by this probe.

sources.claim: Privileged globals are filtered per client; requested interfaces are derived from desktop metadata; fake-input is on the deny list unless declared.
When WaylandServer exists, InputRedirection installs FakeInputBackend.
authenticate marks the device authenticated; absolute pointer and key requests emit KWin input-device events.
Absolute pointer positions are processed as compositor coordinates and then delivered through pointer input processing.

next: Instrument actual pointer enter/motion delivery to both the host surface and popup surface, and verify the private output geometry/cursor position before claiming the UI received input.
After the input route is proven, repeat only the necessary search focus and category-hover sequence; record event ordering for visible/activeFocus/currentIndex/child popup/deactivation.
